brief.headline: We project the 2026/27 US crop at 11.63m bales (all cotton; upland 11.24m), 1.81m below the October 2026 WASDE (13.44m). Texas drives the gap: 2.99m vs USDA 4.35m, on 52% projected abandonment.
points: BMR-Com crop projection (2026-10-25): US upland 11.24m bales (95% 9.1–13.9m; 99% 8.4–15.0m) vs USDA 13.06m; all cotton 11.63m vs WASDE 13.44m. Texas 2.99m (95% 2.2–4.1m) vs USDA 4.35m, with final Texas abandonment projected at 52% (95% 34–70%) against 34% in USDA's numbers.

Classing by office to Oct 23: South Texas (Corpus Christi) 951k bales classed; West Texas (Lubbock 42k, Lamesa 19k, Abilene 22k) 83k. West Texas, where abandonment decides the crop, has barely started; it is projected from drought and ratings until its classing builds.

Texas FSA failed acres (October release) are 9.8% of planted. Failed acres are reported to FSA with a lag and the December–January releases settle them, so the abandonment projection uses this season's drought and ratings readings against what similar readings meant for final abandonment in past seasons.

Cross-check — Drought model: Texas abandonment 48.6% (±14 pts) from the highest-R² drought model (D1-D4 cumulative, R² 57%, cotton-area drought through 2026-10-20), against 33.9% implied by USDA, at USDA's 535 lb yield: Texas 3.38m bales, US crop 12.47m (±1σ 11.56–13.38m).

Cross-check — Ratings model: Texas condition index 2.50 (latest two weeks) points to 307 lb per planted acre (USDA 354; fit R² 0.82 over 2001–2025): Texas 3.77m bales, US crop 12.86m (±1σ 12.33–13.48m).
Cross-check — Average of the two, Texas 3.58m (USDA 4.35m), US crop 12.67m (±1σ 12.12–13.31m); every other state at USDA's latest.

Balance sheet (WASDE 2026/27, our crop): beginning stocks 4.15m + crop 12.67m + imports 0.01m − mill use 1.50m − exports 12.30m = ending stocks 3.03m (stocks/use 21.9% vs WASDE 27.5%); ±1σ 2.48–3.67m. These stocks drive the price and spread fair values on the model tabs.

Crop-progress cross-check (ratings, drought, FSA failed acres, classing): US upland 13.06m vs USDA 13.06m (+0.0%). It is higher than the drought model because it projects Texas abandonment lower; it would replace the headline only if it proves the better predictor.
Crop ratings: 35% good/excellent and 37% poor/very poor nationally.

Texas abandonment: FSA failed acres are 9.8% of reported plantings so far, but failed acres keep rising after October — on this season's drought and ratings we project final abandonment of 39% (state average 38%), vs 34% implied by USDA. Yield 507 lb vs USDA 535; 54% of Texas in D2–D4 drought.
Largest gaps to USDA: Texas 3.82m vs 4.35m; Oklahoma 0.38m vs 0.19m; South Carolina 0.41m vs 0.33m.
NASS ginnings to Mid Oct (Oct 15, 2026): 1.65m running bales, 12.2% of last season's total (normal 12.6% by this date).

Projection from ginnings: 13.18m bales (±1σ 12.58m–13.80m), +0.9% vs USDA, with 19% of it resting on ginning so far; Texas ginning pace alone points to 3.20m (425 lb on harvested acres after projected abandonment).
2.22m upland bales classed this season through Oct 22, -5% vs the same week last year; normally 14% of the crop is classed by now.

Quality so far: tenderable 86.3% (+8.5 pts vs last year); color 31 & better 69.6% (+18.5 pts vs last year); staple 36.58 (-0.32 vs last year); mike 5.0+ discount 5.5% (-8.0 pts vs last year); strength 31.0 g/tex (-0.3 vs last year).
